newsitem.title: UK: BBC World Service may launch 24 hour news service.
newsitem.headline: BBC World Service may launch 24 hour news service.

text.p: The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) said on Tuesday it wanted to launch a 24-hour global English language radio news service to complement its existing World Service output.
"The World Service has developed a detailed strategy for the next five years, for discussion with government," the BBC said in its 1996/97 annual report.
"The strategy envisages a continuous news and information service in English to be delivered alongside the existing broad mix of English language programmes," it added.
BBC director-general John Birt said the World Service was also exploring the launch of "major new services for the Internet".

Birt urged the new Labour government to adopt a "realistic" approach to funding the World Service. Under the previous government, Britain's Foreign Office last year reversed plans to cut World Service funding by five million pounds ($8.4 million).

The BBC said World Service's global audience increased last year to 143 million weekly listeners from 140 million. The radio service broadcasts in 45 languages and has listeners in some 140 countries around the globe. REUTER
